Question: Why do Americans generally dislike eating organ meat?
Answer: Hmm… Liverwurst, chopped chicken livers, beef tongue, lamb tongue, all the offcuts that go into sausages, chicken gizzards, liver and onions. All of them made frequent appearances on our dinner table when I was growing up. I don't do liver and onions any more because calf’s liver is a bit strongly flavored for my taste, but the rest of them are still on the menu. Other Americans must be eating them too, because they're usually available on the supermarket shelves. Actually, I'm not sure about lamb's tongue. I haven't looked for it in a while. But the rest of them are there.

Question: Would a 11 7/8"Dia.× 2 3/ 8" depth pan work for a turned out pineapple upsidedown cake?
Answer: Most pineapple upside down cake recipes call for an 8″ or 9″ pan. So unless you double the recipe, you will end up with a very thin cake. But the cake part of a classic upside down cake is just a standard yellow sponge. Just look for a recipe for yellow cake that makes two 9″ layers, use about 2/3 - 3/4 of it to make your cake, and use the rest for a few cupcakes on the side. Pretty much any birthday cake recipe will give you enough batter to do that. It's a good idea to butter the bottom of the pan, add a circle of parchment paper in the bottom, then butter the parchment. Makes unmolding the sticky, caramelized cake much easier.

Question: Should you use bread flour for croissants?
Answer: French bread flour averages around 12% protein or slightly higher. US bread flours are usually a little stronger, while most brands of all purpose flour hover around 10.5% - 11.5%. In my experience, I get the best results with a combination of bread flour and all purpose, but that may vary, depending on the brand of flour you use. King Arthur Flour makes an unbleached AP flour that has 12% protein, and is very nice for croissants.

Question: What is the correct word, "fresh baked bread" or "freshly baked bread"?
Answer: Fresh is an adjective that describes the state of the bread (a noun), so the proper phrase would be fresh bread. If you want to describe how recently the bread was baked, you would use freshly, an adverb that describes the verb baked. Freshly baked bread is grammatically correct in that case.

Question: What did the average American family eat before immigrants from Italy and other countries brought over pizza, pasta, chili, and other food?
Answer: Well, Italian immigrants didn't bring us chili. And there were plenty of immigrants from other countries before the Italians arrived, along with hundreds of Native American tribes, all of whom had their own individual cuisine. There was a large influx of Italian immigrants to the US between 1900 and 1915 -- at approximately 3 million individuals, they were the largest group of immigrants at that time, the majority from southern Italy. They had a decided impact on American cooking. And American ingredients changed the way they made their traditional foods. But they were far from the first group that did that, and American cooking was as varied as the countries its settlers came from. Early American cookbooks have a decided English influence, but food was very regional in those days. There would have been Dutch and German food in the northeast, a burgeoning southern cuisine influenced by both Native American cooking and that of African slaves, and other cuisines brought to the new world by other settlers. The beginning of the twentieth century is actually fairly late in rhe development of American cuisine. An average family would have eaten what was produced in their local area, influenced by their cultural heritage, so its difficult to define exactly what kind of food they would have eaten. But the US had a number of vibrant food cultures long before the influx of Italian immigrants reached its shores.
